content:
Each box \(ABC\) can only serve sheets \(AB, AC, BC\), so one box serves at most \(3\) sheets. Hence at least  
\[
\left\lceil \frac{100}{3}\right\rceil = 34
\]
boxes are needed.

Now show \(34\) suffice. Label the digits \(1,\dots,9\) as the points of a \(3\times 3\) affine plane over \(\mathbb F_3\). Its \(12\) lines are:
\[
\{1,2,3\},\{4,5,6\},\{7,8,9\},
\{1,4,7\},\{2,5,8\},\{3,6,9\},
\{1,5,9\},\{2,6,7\},\{3,4,8\},
\{1,6,8\},\{2,4,9\},\{3,5,7\}.
\]
For each line \(\{a,b,c\}\), use the two boxes \(abc\) and \(cba\). These \(24\) boxes cover every ordered pair among digits \(1,\dots,9\), since any two digits lie on exactly one line and the two orientations give both orders.

Finally add the \(10\) boxes
\[
010,\ 101,\ 202,\ 303,\ 404,\ 505,\ 606,\ 707,\ 808,\ 909.
\]
These cover all sheets involving digit \(0\), including all loops \(00,11,\dots,99\).

Thus \(24+10=34\) boxes suffice, and the minimum is
\[
\boxed{34}.
\]
